claim: Glycan-binding proteins, called lectins, are exposed on mammalian cell surfaces and decipher the information encoded within glycans translating it into biochemical signal transduction pathways in the cell.
source: Glycan-binding proteins, so-called lectins, are exposed on mammalian cell surfaces and decipher the information encoded within glycans translating it into biochemical signal transduction pathways in the cell.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about lectin function in mammalian cells.

claim: All receptors transmit information with similar signaling capacity, except dectin-2.
source: All receptors transmit information with similar signaling capacity, except dectin-2.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing channel capacities across multiple receptors shown in the manuscript.

claim: Dectin-2 was identified to be less efficient in information transmission compared to the other CTLs.
source: This lectin was identified to be less efficient in information transmission compared to the other CTLs
evidence: This is supported by channel capacity measurements presented in the manuscript comparing dectin-2 to other CTLs.

claim: When the sensitivity of the dectin-2 pathway was enhanced by overexpression of its co-receptor FcRγ, its transmitted information was not increased.
source: even when the sensitivity of the dectin-2 pathway was enhanced by overexpression of its co-receptor FcRγ, its transmitted information was not.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing FcRγ overexpression effects on dectin-2 signaling.

claim: The signaling capacity of lectin receptors using a similar signal transduction pathway (dectin-1 and dectin-2) is integrated by compromising between the lectins.
source: We show how the signaling capacity of lectin receptors using a similar signal transduction pathway (dectin-1 and dectin-2) is being integrated by compromising between the lectins.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing intermediate channel capacity and EC50 values when both receptors are co-expressed.

claim: Co-expression of MCL synergistically enhanced the dectin-2 signaling capacity, particularly at low-glycan stimulant concentration.
source: In contrast, co-expression of MCL synergistically enhanced the dectin-2 signaling capacity, particularly at low-glycan stimulant concentration.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing increased channel capacity when MCL is co-expressed with dectin-2.

claim: Glycans are present in all living cells and play a key role in many essential biological processes including development, differentiation, and immunity.
source: Glycans are present in all living cells and play a key role in many essential biological processes including development, differentiation, and immunity.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature (Bode et al., 2019; Maverakis et al., 2015; Williams, 2017).

claim: Glycans often encode for information in cellular communication such as self-/non-self-discrimination, cellular identity, and homing as well as apoptosis markers.
source: Being surface exposed, glycans often encode for information in cellular communication such as self-/non-self-discrimination, cellular identity, and homing as well as apoptosis markers (Bode et al., 2019; Maverakis et al., 2015; Williams, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Glycans are branched structures, where subtle changes in the glycosidic bonds between each monomer can carry essential pieces of information.
source: Other than linear biopolymers, such as proteins and nucleic acids, glycans are branched structures, where subtle changes in the glycosidic bonds between each monomer can carry essential pieces of information.
evidence: This is established knowledge about glycan structure and function.

claim: Glycans are products of large cellular machinery and are therefore not directly encoded by the genome.
source: Adding to this complexity, glycans are products of large cellular machinery and are therefore not directly encoded by the genome (Cummings, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: No glycan is recognized by a single receptor, and no individual lectin is highly specific for only one glycan.
source: Glycans are recognized by lectins, yet no glycan is recognized by a single receptor, and no individual lectin is highly specific for only one glycan.
evidence: This is established knowledge about glycan-lectin interactions.

claim: Glycan-lectin interactions often depend on the multivalency of both the receptor and the ligand.
source: Additionally, affinities are low, and interactions often depend on the multivalency of both the receptor and the ligand.
evidence: This is established knowledge about glycan-lectin binding characteristics.

claim: Glycan lectin communication should be considered as a stochastically behaving system, rather than a deterministic one.
source: Overall, since alterations of the glycocalyx do not function as a deterministic on/off switch but rather a progressive tuning of the cellular response, glycan lectin communication should be considered as a stochastically behaving system, rather than a deterministic one (Dennis, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation and represents an inference about the nature of glycan-lectin communication.

claim: Many lectin receptors serve as triggers for multiple immunological signaling pathways, often funneling down to NF-κB as a transcription factor.
source: Many lectin receptors serve as triggers for multiple immunological signaling pathways, often funneling down to NF-κB (nuclear factor kappa-B) as a transcription factor.
evidence: This is established knowledge about lectin receptor signaling.

claim: MINCLE is a CTL involved in the recognition of pathogens as well as self-damage.
source: MINCLE (macrophage-inducible C-type lectin), for example, is a CTL involved in the recognition of pathogens as well as self-damage (Miyake et al., 2015; Williams, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MINCLE and dectin-2 signal via the FcRγ gamma chain.
source: MINCLE and its close relative dectin-2 (dendritic cell-associated C-type lectin-2) signal via the FcRγ gamma chain (Miyake et al., 2015; Ostrop et al., 2015; Sato et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MINCLE and dectin-2 signaling leads to CARD9-BCL-10-Malt1 activation.
source: MINCLE and its close relative dectin-2 (dendritic cell-associated C-type lectin-2) signal via the FcRγ gamma chain (Miyake et al., 2015; Ostrop et al., 2015; Sato et al., 2006), leading to CARD9-BCL-10-Malt1 activation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: CARD9-BCL-10-Malt1 activation results in the activation of NF-κB, eventually triggering cytokine release.
source: This in turn results in the activation of NF-κB, eventually triggering cytokine release.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the signaling cascade downstream of CARD9-BCL-10-Malt1.

claim: Dectin-2 and MINCLE share the same signal transduction pathway, while having different functions.
source: Importantly, these two receptors share the same signal transduction pathway, while having different functions (Thompson et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Dectin-1 and dectin-2 have different signal transduction pathways.
source: In contrast, dectin-1 and dectin-2 have different signal transduction pathways but are both involved in the detection of β-glucans and mannan, respectively (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is illustrated in Figure 1A and represents established knowledge.

claim: Dectin-1 is involved in the detection of β-glucans.
source: In contrast, dectin-1 and dectin-2 have different signal transduction pathways but are both involved in the detection of β-glucans and mannan, respectively (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about dectin-1 ligand specificity.

claim: Dectin-2 is involved in the detection of mannan.
source: In contrast, dectin-1 and dectin-2 have different signal transduction pathways but are both involved in the detection of β-glucans and mannan, respectively (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about dectin-2 ligand specificity.

claim: FurFurMan, mannan, and invertase initiated dectin-2 signaling in reporter cells.
source: FurFurMan, an extract of Malassezia furfur, as well as the polysaccharide mannan and invertase, both from Saccharomyces cerevisiae, initiated dectin-2 signaling.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C-E.

claim: Mannose itself could not initiate dectin-2 signaling but was able to inhibit dectin-2 function.
source: In contrast, owing to the lack of multivalency, mannose itself could not initiate signaling but was able to inhibit dectin-2 function (Figure 1C and D, and also Appendix 1—figure 1 A; Ishikawa et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and citation to prior literature.

claim: Invertase treated with α-mannosidase does not activate the NF-κB signaling.
source: In parallel, the invertase treated with α-mannosidase does not activate the NF-κB signaling, indicating the glycosylation-dependent dectin-2 activity (Appendix 1—figure 1 B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 1 B.

claim: The activation of human dectin-2 receptor is triggered by Man-α1–2 Man moieties presented on scaffolds like proteins, glycans, or polystyrene beads.
source: The activation of human dectin-2 receptor is in line with previous reports on its murine homolog, which is triggered by Man-α1–2 Man moieties presented on scaffolds like proteins, glycans, or polystyrene beads (Ishikawa et al., 2013; Yonekawa et al., 2014; Zhou et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: FurFurMan could stimulate dectin-1 cells, but this was not inhibited by the addition of mannose.
source: However, while FurFurMan could also stimulate dectin-1 cells, this was not inhibited by the addition of mannose, which is expected for this β-glucan receptor (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The cellular population revealed an overlap between the unstimulated and the maximally stimulated population, demonstrating the absence of a clear two-state behavior on a population level.
source: The cellular population revealed an overlap between the unstimulated and the maximally stimulated population, demonstrating the absence of a clear two-state behavior on a population level (Figure 1E, Appendix 1—figure 1 C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and Appendix 1—figure 1 C.

claim: GFP expression required at least 16 hr of stimulation to reach its maximum in steady-state protein expression.
source: To ensure that change in the reporter level is not affected by protein expression rate, we confirmed that GFP expression required at least 16 hr of stimulation to reach its maximum in steady-state protein expression, while short stimulation with for 2–6 hr does not lead the maximum level of GFP production (Appendix 1—figure 1 D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 1 D.

claim: Short stimulation for 2–6 hr does not lead to the maximum level of GFP production.
source: To ensure that change in the reporter level is not affected by protein expression rate, we confirmed that GFP expression required at least 16 hr of stimulation to reach its maximum in steady-state protein expression, while short stimulation with for 2–6 hr does not lead the maximum level of GFP production (Appendix 1—figure 1 D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 1 D.

claim: When dectin-2 expressing cells sorted according to their GFP expression level were re-stimulated, both populations again showed the same broad GFP expression.
source: We also ruled out any influence of the selection process for the cellular clones, by sorting dectin-2 expressing cells according to their GFP expression level. When re-stimulated, both populations again showed the same broad GFP expression, confirming the wide range of the response to be independent of genetic differences between individual cells (Appendix 1—figure 1 E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 1 E.

claim: The wide range of the response is independent of genetic differences between individual cells.
source: When re-stimulated, both populations again showed the same broad GFP expression, confirming the wide range of the response to be independent of genetic differences between individual cells (Appendix 1—figure 1 E).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing similar broad GFP expression in sorted populations.

claim: Previous work on TNF-α signaling found the TNF-α channel to have a channel capacity of about 1 bit, in particular 1.64 bits when a reporter cell system was used.
source: Previous work on TNF-α signaling found the TNF-α channel to have a channel capacity of about 1 bit in particular 1.64 bits when a reporter cell system was used (Cheong et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Channel capacity can be further increased if one can measure the temporal evolution of output dynamics instead of static output dataset.
source: In addition, this channel capacity can be further increased if one can measure the temporal evolution of output dynamics instead of static output dataset (Selimkhanov et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: For U937 cells, TNFαR transmits 1.34 bits of channel capacity for TNF-α stimulant.
source: For U937 cells, we found the TNFαR transmits 1.34 bits of channel capacity for TNF-α stimulant (Figure 2A and B)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: TNFαR channel capacity was not influenced by the introduction of additional lectins (i.e. MINCLE, dectin-2, and DC-SIGN).
source: For U937 cells, we found the TNFαR transmits 1.34 bits of channel capacity for TNF-α stimulant (Figure 2A and B), which was not influenced by the introduction of additional lectins (i.e. MINCLE, dectin-2, and DC-SIGN, see Appendix 1—figure 2 C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 2 C.

claim: For dectin-1 expressing U937 cells, the channel capacities were 1.20 and 1.09 bits for depleted zymosan (DZ) and FurFurMan input, respectively.
source: In the case of dectin-1 expressing U937 cells, the channel capacities were 1.20 and 1.09 bits for depleted zymosan (DZ) and FurFurMan input, respectively
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: MINCLE had a channel capacity of 0.98 bits.
source: while both MINCLE and TLR1&2 had a channel capacity of 0.98 and 0.99 bits, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TLR1&2 had a channel capacity of 0.99 bits.
source: while both MINCLE and TLR1&2 had a channel capacity of 0.98 and 0.99 bits, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Dectin-2 stimulation resulted in a channel capacity of 0.70 bits using FurFurMan as a ligand.
source: In contrast, dectin-2 stimulation resulted in a channel capacity of 0.70 bits using FurFurMan as a ligand.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Stimulation using heat inactivated invertase had 0.80 bits channel capacity.
source: Stimulation using heat inactivated invertase or mannan had 0.80 and 0.49 bits, respectively (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Stimulation using mannan had 0.49 bits channel capacity.
source: Stimulation using heat inactivated invertase or mannan had 0.80 and 0.49 bits, respectively (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In THP-1 cells, a similar trend of lower GFP expression upon stimulation is observed for dectin-2 compared to TNFαR.
source: Also, in THP-1 cells, a similar trend of lower GFP expression upon stimulation is observed, further supporting the notion that dectin-2 has a lower signal transmission capacity compared to the other receptors such as TNFαR (Appendix 1—figure 2 D-F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 2 D-F.

claim: The substantial differences between the channel capacities of MINCLE and dectin-2 rely on very early ligand recognition events.
source: The most striking difference was found between MINCLE and dectin-2, as both lectins use the same signaling pathway via FcRγ (Ishikawa et al., 2013), suggesting that the substantial differences between the channel capacities rely on very early ligand recognition events.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that MINCLE and dectin-2 use the same signaling pathway but have different channel capacities.

claim: Overexpression of FcRγ resulted in at least twofold increase of NF-κB controlled GFP expression.
source: The overexpression of FcRγ resulted in at least twofold increase of NF-κB controlled GFP expression (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Overexpression of both dectin-2 and FcRγ yielded a high-basal NF-κB activation of the cells.
source: Overexpression of both dectin-2 and FcRγ yielded a high-basal NF-κB activation of the cells while the sensitivity for its ligand (EC50) increased about 50-fold.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Overexpression of both dectin-2 and FcRγ increased the sensitivity for its ligand (EC50) about 50-fold.
source: Overexpression of both dectin-2 and FcRγ yielded a high-basal NF-κB activation of the cells while the sensitivity for its ligand (EC50) increased about 50-fold.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: While the maximal GFP signal of dectin-2 (MFI) was increased in the presence of FcRγ overexpression, the channel capacity decreased simultaneously (0.41 bits).
source: While the maximal GFP signal of dectin-2 (MFI, mean fluorescence intensity) was increased in the presence of FcRγ overexpression, the channel capacity however decreased simultaneously (0.41 bits; Figure 2 C–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-E.

claim: Competition with mannose reduced the high-basal NF-κB activation effect in FcRγ overexpressing dectin-2 cells.
source: Since competition with mannose reduced this effect, we speculate that decreased channel capacity might originate from self-recognition of dectin-2 of ligands being present either on the same cell or those in close proximity during the culture conditions (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Decreased channel capacity in FcRγ overexpressing dectin-2 cells might originate from self-recognition of dectin-2 of ligands being present either on the same cell or those in close proximity during the culture conditions.
source: Since competition with mannose reduced this effect, we speculate that decreased channel capacity might originate from self-recognition of dectin-2 of ligands being present either on the same cell or those in close proximity during the culture conditions (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that mannose competition reduces the effect.

claim: The channel capacity of a glycan-based communication channel is not necessarily coupled to its sensitivity.
source: From this, we concluded the channel capacity of a glycan-based communication channel is not necessarily coupled to its sensitivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing FcRγ overexpression increases sensitivity but decreases channel capacity.

claim: The ability of a communication channel to transmit information is not well described by its maximal signal alone (i.e. MFI), but rather by the channel capacity.
source: Also, the ability of a communication channel to transmit information is not well described by its maximal signal alone (i.e. MFI), but rather by the channel capacity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The difference in MINCLE and dectin-2 channel capacities is not due to differences in receptor expression levels.
source: Next, we quantified the number of receptors and excluded that the difference in MINCLE and dectin-2 channel capacities is due to differences in receptor expression levels (Appendix 1—figure 2 G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 2 G.

claim: The number of receptors has little influence on the channel capacity or amplitude.
source: Taken together, dectin-2 has relatively less channel capacity, and while its sensitivity (EC50) can be modulated with FcRγ, the transmitted information does not increase. Additionally, the number of receptors has little influence on the channel capacity or amplitude.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The level of receptor expression did not change upon expression of an additional lectin.
source: First of all, we found that the level of receptor expression did not change upon expression of an additional lectin (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Dectin-1 expressing cells gave a higher maximal signal (i.e. maximal MFI) and channel capacity than dectin-2 expressing cells.
source: Dectin-1 expressing cells gave a higher maximal signal (i.e. maximal MFI) and channel capacity than dectin-2 expressing cells; however, the latter channel showed higher sensitivity (EC50) to FurFurMan.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Dectin-2 expressing cells showed higher sensitivity (EC50) to FurFurMan than dectin-1 expressing cells.
source: Dectin-1 expressing cells gave a higher maximal signal (i.e. maximal MFI) and channel capacity than dectin-2 expressing cells; however, the latter channel showed higher sensitivity (EC50) to FurFurMan.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The double positive cells (dectin-1 and dectin-2) did compromise between the two receptors, displaying the values corresponding to the intermediate values of the EC50 and channel capacity of dectin-1 and dectin-2.
source: We found that the double positive cells did compromise between the two receptors, displaying the values corresponding to the intermediate values of the EC50 and channel capacity of dectin-1 and dectin-2 (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: U937 dectin-1 dectin-2 expressing cells showed the same dose-response curve as dectin-1 expressing cells when mannose was used to interfere with dectin-2 signaling.
source: Additionally, mannose could be used to interfere with dectin-2 signaling, thus U937 dectin-1 dectin-2 expressing cells showed the same dose-response curve as dectin-1 expressing cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: When DZ, a dectin-1 specific stimulant, was used, dectin-2 expression did not significantly influence the response of the double positive cells.
source: When DZ, a dectin-1 specific stimulants, was used, dectin-2 expression did not significantly influence the response of the double positive cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data mentioned in the manuscript.

claim: Dectin-2 specific signaling was not influenced by dectin-1 expression.
source: Hence, dectin-2 specific signaling was not influenced by dectin-1 expression (Appendix 1—figure 3 A-C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 3 A-C.

claim: Inhibition of dectin-2 signaling initiated by FurFurMan by the addition of 25 mM mannose resulted in a response that was not a compromise.
source: Moreover, inhibition of dectin-2 signaling initiated by FurFurMan by the addition of 25 mM mannose resulted a response that was not a compromise.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The simultaneous stimulation of dectin-1 and dectin-2 resulted in a compromise between their channels.
source: Taken together, we see that the simultaneous stimulation of dectin-1 and dectin-2 resulted in a compromise between their channels, which demonstrates how these two channels integrate glycan signal into response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: DC-SIGN does not elicit NF-κB signaling by itself in U937 cells.
source: Although DC-SIGN does not elicit NF-κB signaling by itself in U937 cells, it is known to recognize high-mannose structures present on invertase (Gringhuis et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and citation to prior literature.

claim: DC-SIGN is known to recognize high-mannose structures present on invertase.
source: Although DC-SIGN does not elicit NF-κB signaling by itself in U937 cells, it is known to recognize high-mannose structures present on invertase (Gringhuis et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: U937 dectin-2 DC-SIGN cells experience significantly increased ligand binding.
source: As expected, U937 dectin-2 DC-SIGN cells experience significantly increased ligand binding (Appendix 1—figure 4 A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 4 A and B.

claim: DC-SIGN-mediated ligand binding did not alter the dectin-2 channel capacity for FurFurMan or invertase stimulation.
source: In fact, DC-SIGN-mediated ligand binding did not alter the dectin-2 channel capacity for FurFurMan or invertase stimulation or did DC-SIGN expression itself modulate TLR4 signaling (Figure 4B, Appendix 1—figure 4 C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Appendix 1—figure 4 C.

claim: DC-SIGN expression itself did not modulate TLR4 signaling.
source: In fact, DC-SIGN-mediated ligand binding did not alter the dectin-2 channel capacity for FurFurMan or invertase stimulation or did DC-SIGN expression itself modulate TLR4 signaling (Figure 4B, Appendix 1—figure 4 C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 4 C.

claim: The sensitivity, as assessed by EC50, increased for dectin-2 DC-SIGN expressing cells.
source: However, the sensitivity, as assessed by EC50, increased for dectin-2 DC-SIGN expressing cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Overexpression of MCL significantly increased the channel capacity of dectin-2 expressing cells, particularly when limiting the dataset to low-maximum invertase concentrations.
source: Contrary to DC-SIGN, overexpression of MCL significantly increased the channel capacity of dectin-2 expressing cells, particularly when limiting our dataset to low-maximum invertase concentrations (Figure 4B and D, Appendix 1—figure 4 D and E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and D, and Appendix 1—figure 4 D and E.

claim: MCL enhances the fidelity of invertase information transmission of dectin-2 channel.
source: This indicates that MCL enhances the fidelity of invertase information transmission of dectin-2 channel, providing quantitative measurement of synergistic effect of MCL (Ostrop et al., 2015; Zhu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing increased channel capacity with MCL co-expression, supported by citations.

claim: TNFαR has a nanomolar affinity for its ligand.
source: Since TNFαR has a nanomolar affinity for its ligand (Grell et al., 1998), we applied an anti-dectin-2 antibody to stimulate dectin-2 cells.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Stimulation of dectin-2 cells with an anti-dectin-2 antibody did not result in an increase in channel capacity.
source: Since TNFαR has a nanomolar affinity for its ligand (Grell et al., 1998), we applied an anti-dectin-2 antibody to stimulate dectin-2 cells. Even under these conditions, we did not monitor an increase in channel capacity (Appendix 1—figure 4 F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 4 F.

claim: MCL but not DC-SIGN significantly increase the dectin-2 channel capacity.
source: Therefore, we found that MCL but not DC-SIGN significantly increase the dectin-2 channel capacity, while both MCL and DC-SIGN enhance cellular binding of the stimulants and the resulting cellular sensitivity to invertase.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Both MCL and DC-SIGN enhance cellular binding of the stimulants and the resulting cellular sensitivity to invertase.
source: Therefore, we found that MCL but not DC-SIGN significantly increase the dectin-2 channel capacity, while both MCL and DC-SIGN enhance cellular binding of the stimulants and the resulting cellular sensitivity to invertase.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TNFαR, MINCLE, and dectin-1 have a similar level of noise power.
source: TNFaR, MINCLE, and dectin-1 have a similar level of noise power.
evidence: This is supported by the signal and noise power analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: TNFαR shows the highest signal power amongst TNFαR, MINCLE, and dectin-1.
source: Amongst the three receptors, TNFaR shows the highest signal power and consequently the highest signal-to-noise ratio (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: TNFαR shows the highest signal-to-noise ratio amongst TNFαR, MINCLE, and dectin-1.
source: Amongst the three receptors, TNFaR shows the highest signal power and consequently the highest signal-to-noise ratio (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: TNFαR, MINCLE, and dectin-1 have a signal-to-noise ratio higher than one.
source: All three channels have a signal-to-noise ratio higher than one.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: For dectin-2, both signal and noise power are low compared to the other receptors.
source: For dectin-2, both signal and noise power are low compared to the other receptors; however, the noise power exceeds the signal power, resulting in a significantly lower signal-to-noise ratio.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: For dectin-2, the noise power exceeds the signal power, resulting in a significantly lower signal-to-noise ratio.
source: For dectin-2, both signal and noise power are low compared to the other receptors; however, the noise power exceeds the signal power, resulting in a significantly lower signal-to-noise ratio.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: The lower variation of the mean GFP expression (i.e. signal power) of dectin-2 dictates the reduced channel capacity compared to the other receptors.
source: Since the signal power is independent of the noise power, our data indicate that the lower variation of the mean GFP expression (i.e. signal power) of dectin-2 dictates the reduced channel capacity compared to the other receptors.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the signal and noise power analysis.

claim: When dectin-1 and dectin-2 were co-expressed, both the signal and the noise power were compromised.
source: Analogous to the compromised channel capacity when dectin-1 and dectin-2 were co-expressed (Figure 3C), the analysis revealed that both the signal and the noise power were compromised as well (Appendix 1—figure 5 A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 5 A and B.

claim: In case of FcRγ overexpression, dectin-2 signaling after invertase stimulation is characterized by increased noise power, resulting in decreased signal-to-noise ratio.
source: In case of FcRγ overexpression, dectin-2 signaling after invertase stimulation is characterized by increased noise power, resulting in decreased signal-to-noise ratio (Appendix 1—figure 5 C-E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 5 C-E.

claim: The overexpression of FcRγ did not increase the signal power but instead elevated the noise power, leading to reduced channel capacity.
source: Therefore, despite the high-GFP expression at high-stimulant concentrations (Figure 2C), the overexpression of FcRγ, as additional signaling hubs, involved in the dectin-2/NF-κB cascade did not increase the signal power but instead elevated the noise power, leading to reduced channel capacity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the signal and noise power analysis.

claim: The relatively low-channel capacity of dectin-2 is directly related to its low-signal power.
source: Taken together, the relatively low-channel capacity of dectin-2 is directly related to its low-signal power, and the overexpression of FcRγ further decreases the channel capacity through increasing the noise power.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the signal and noise power analysis.

claim: For the receptors other than dectin-2, the channel capacities were around 1 bit or higher.
source: For the receptors other than dectin-2, the channel capacities were around 1 bit or higher, similar values that have been reported for other systems previously (Suderman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and citation to prior literature.

claim: TNF-α receptor has a channel capacity of 1.64±0.36 bits in a comparable reporter cell system.
source: In particular, TNF-α receptor has a channel capacity of 1.64±0.36 bits, which was found in a comparable reporter cell system (Cheong et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The number of receptors expressed on the cell surface did not determine the channel capacity of a signaling channel.
source: Interestingly, the number of receptors expressed on the cell surface did not determine the channel capacity of a signaling channel (Appendix 1—figure 2 G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 2 G.

claim: Lectin signaling pathways and especially the dectin-2 pathway should not be viewed as a deterministic on/off-switch, but rather as difference in the probability of cells to be active at a certain dose.
source: Our results exemplify that lectin signaling pathways and especially the dectin-2 pathway should not be viewed as a deterministic on/off-switch, but rather as difference in the probability of cells to be active at a certain dose.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations of broad population distributions.

claim: Dectin-2 and dectin-1 recognize different epitopes on FurFurMan.
source: Dectin-2 and dectin-1 recognize different epitopes on FurFurMan, and we found that the effects were not additive, but a compromise between the two receptors, showing intermediate sensitivity (EC50) and channel capacity between dectin-2 and dectin-1 (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and established knowledge about receptor specificities.

claim: At high concentrations of FurFurMan the dectin-2 channel is actively inhibiting dectin-1 signaling, resulting in a lower cellular NF-κB activation.
source: This effect implies at high concentrations of FurFurMan the dectin-2 channel is actively inhibiting dectin-1 signaling, resulting in a lower cellular NF-κB activation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of compromised signaling in double positive cells.

claim: Lectins are able to modulate the signals of other receptors.
source: It is well known that lectins are able to modulate the signals of other receptors (Geijtenbeek and Gringhuis, 2009; Gringhuis et al., 2009; Miyake et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: During a fungal infection, exposing multiple epitopes of pathogens are recognized by the precise arsenal of immune receptors, and their underlying signaling pathways are integrating the information contained within the epitopes.
source: Hence, it is likely that during a fungal infection, exposing multiple epitopes of pathogens are recognized by the precise arsenal of immune receptors, and their underlying signaling pathways are integrating the information contained within the epitopes.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental findings about signal integration.

claim: Signal integration leads to a compromise of all activated receptors and results in a specifically tailored biochemical response of the given immune cell.
source: This in turn leads to a compromise of all activated receptors and results in a specifically tailored biochemical response of the given immune cell (Ostrop and Lang, 2017).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: It is likely the receptor itself determines very early on the information flow into the cell.
source: Dectin-2 itself we found to have relatively less channel capacity when compared to the closely related MINCLE that uses the same pathway with more signal power (Figure 2A and B). It is therefore likely the receptor itself determines very early on the information flow into the cell.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that MINCLE and dectin-2 have different channel capacities despite using the same pathway.

claim: The difference in channel capacity between MINCLE and dectin-2 could be a result of MINCLE being stimulated with crystalline insoluble ligands which could result in larger signaling clusters at the cellular surface.
source: This could be a result of MINCLE being stimulated with crystalline insoluble ligands which could result in larger signaling clusters at the cellular surface.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism underlying the difference in channel capacity.

claim: Dectin-2 signaling could be influenced by mannose structures that are present on the cellular surface by giving rise to background signaling and selection for reducing signaling power in an in vitro setting of high-cellular density.
source: Alternatively, dectin-2 signaling could be influenced by mannose structures that are present on the cellular surface by giving rise to background signaling and selection for reducing signaling power in an in vitro setting of high-cellular density.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism underlying the low channel capacity of dectin-2.

claim: Since dectin-2 binds high-mannose structures of eukaryotic origin, a too sensitive reaction might lead to permanent self-recognition of human Man9 structures and hence potential autoimmune reactions.
source: Additionally, since dectin-2 binds high-mannose structures of eukaryotic origin (McGreal et al., 2006), a too sensitive reaction might lead to permanent self-recognition of human Man9 structures for example and hence potential autoimmune reactions.
evidence: This is a speculation supported by citation about dectin-2 ligand specificity.

claim: The dectin-2-dependent high-basal activity of FcRγ overexpressing dectin-2 cells is responsible for a lower channel capacity in dectin-2 FcRγ cells.
source: This hypothesis is supported by the dectin-2-dependent high-basal activity of FcRγ overexpressing dectin-2 cells, which in turn is responsible for a lower channel capacity in dectin-2 FcRγ cells (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Dectin-2 could have evolved to use the CARD9-BCL-10-Malt1 pathway to NF-κB less effectively.
source: Hence, dectin-2 could have evolved to use the CARD9-BCL-10-Malt1 pathway to NF-κB less effective.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental findings.

claim: CTLs are in general becoming more important in autoimmunity.
source: Along the same lines, recent reports show that CTLs are in general becoming more important in autoimmunity, dectin-2 in particular is known to be responsible for the development of allergic reactions (Dambuza and Brown, 2015; Parsons et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Dectin-2 in particular is known to be responsible for the development of allergic reactions.

evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Human monocytes and dectin-2 positive U937 cells have comparable receptor densities.
source: Human monocytes and dectin-2 positive U937 cells have comparable receptor densities and respond similar to stimulation with zymosan particles (Appendix 1—figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Appendix 1—figure 6A and B.

claim: Human monocytes and dectin-2 positive U937 cells respond similarly to stimulation with zymosan particles.

claim: Channel capacity calculations are applicable regardless of the nature of signal and medium.
source: Importantly, since our channel capacity calculations are applicable regardless of the nature of signal and medium, one could use it to quantify cellular responses in similar assays in the future.
evidence: This is a statement about the general applicability of the channel capacity metric.
